principles: Mechanical isolation over instructions: mkdtemp non-git roots + voiding assertions, never discipline alone
Resume-safe execution: identity-keyed cells, append-only records, re-runnable without double-counting
Replay before trust: every archived run dir re-scores byte-identically before any statistic is computed
Bounded pilot spend: smallest corpus satisfying plan section 7 preconditions
drivers: M7 cannot start without the frozen N and the committed runner
Leakage audit is a stopping-rule item (plan 11.3) — must be mechanical and repeatable
Shared token budget: pilot must not balloon into a powered run

options.name: committed-runner-adapted-from-scratch-pattern
pros: RUN-RECORD contract already fixes the output shape
One command with --plan dry-run and resume
cons: Adaptation work for the experience-ablation cell shape

options.name: ad-hoc-shell-pilot
cons: Unreproducible, no resume, nothing committed — fails the M6 exit criterion outright

options.name: generalize-recovery-runner-into-shared-framework
cons: Scope creep; touches proven scratch; plan asks only for a committed runner for this experiment

rationale: Only the committed adapted runner satisfies the M6 exit criterion (campaign runner committed) while reusing the resume/identity-key mechanics proven by the 49h recovery campaign; the RUN-RECORD.md contract from M4 already pins its output anatomy so score.mjs works unchanged, and --plan/resume keep real-host spend bounded and interruptible.

preMortem.scenario: A pilot arm-run executes with the repo (or a git worktree) as cwd so resolveLearningRoot lands on the production store; lessons from experiment tasks contaminate production analytics
preMortem.trigger: Runner forgets mkdtemp isolation or copies the fixture into a git-tracked path
preMortem.consequence: Store-isolation breach — stopping-rule violation, pilot voided
preMortem.mitigation: Runner asserts the resolved root per run (observability_snapshot resolvedLearningRoot) BEFORE host execution; score.mjs voids on production storeRoot; exit criterion counts voided records = 0

preMortem.scenario: Control-arm host reconstructs a trap answer from residue in the fixture tree, biasing the pilot toward null and freezing a wrong N
preMortem.trigger: Generator leaks strip-list content into workspace/ or prompt.md
preMortem.consequence: Baseline estimate invalid; M7 sized wrongly; leakage discovered late voids the powered run
preMortem.mitigation: leakage-audit.mjs runs BEFORE any host run as a hard precondition in run-pilot.mjs; audit failure aborts the pilot

preMortem.scenario: Pilot interrupted mid-run (session death, token exhaustion) and a naive rerun double-counts cells or reorders execution
preMortem.trigger: No identity-keyed resume or order not committed
preMortem.consequence: Pair ledger inconsistent; run order tunable after outcomes — pre-registration broken
preMortem.mitigation: Cells keyed by (experimentId, fixtureId, arm); terminal run.json marks completion; run order derives from the committed seed; resume skips terminal cells only

preMortem.scenario: The control-arm defect baseline lands outside the planning band (0.5-0.8) or the Wilson CI is wider than 0.30 at 15 runs
preMortem.consequence: Freezing N anyway would misSize M7
preMortem.mitigation: pilotFreezeCheck enforces the CI-width gate; the runner supports adding control-arm fault runs incrementally; out-of-band baseline triggers the documented recompute path instead of a silent freeze

preMortem.scenario: Host CLI invocation shape wrong (flags/permissions), burning tokens on runs that produce unscoreable dirs
preMortem.mitigation: Single smoke cell (one fixture, one arm) validated end-to-end (run dir -> score.mjs emits non-voided record) before enumerating the full pilot; --plan dry-run reviewed first
